title: We want to expand into Romania and Bulgaria but our sales team of five people has no experience with public procurement rules there — we have lost two tenders already because we submitted the wrong notarial documents and missed a local-content clause we did not know existed.

record.text: We want to expand into Romania and Bulgaria but our sales team of five people has no experience with public procurement rules there — we have lost two tenders already because we submitted the wrong notarial documents and missed a local-content clause we did not know existed.
record.detail: We want to sell our RTU and control panel products directly to municipal utilities in Romania and Bulgaria rather than through local resellers who take a large margin. Both countries run public tenders through their national e-procurement portals. We have a sales team of five, all experienced with Serbian and regional procurement under UNCITRAL-style rules, but Romanian and Bulgarian tender documents use different notarial certification formats, translated attestation requirements, and, in two tenders we entered, local-content or EU-origin documentation we were not aware of. We lost both tenders on administrative grounds before technical evaluation even started. We do not have a local legal partner in either country yet. We have budget for a short consultancy engagement and we are willing to pay a success fee on a first contract win. What we need is either a structured guide to the documentation requirements for each country, or a contact who can review our tender packs before submission. A realistic target is winning one contract in Romania or Bulgaria within 18 months.
